correctness.rationale: The one-variable Carathéodory parametrization is an equivalence for all -pi/2<beta<pi/2. Expanding the exponential primitive yields the exact determinant identity, checked by 27 independent rational coefficient specializations. The two-step Schur parametrization exhausts all possible first three moments. Maximizing the last parameter and cos(theta) gives a decreasing three-regime threshold and an explicit sharp branch optimum 33/16, with positive degree-ten Bernstein certificate for the only auxiliary inequality. An explicit degree-two Blaschke factor attains this moment bound. |c_n|<=2 gives a uniform remainder <=cos(beta)/18+cos(beta)^2/9 after normalization, and the same witness proves the reverse bound, hence the sharp two-sided limit. Computations are supplementary rather than a substitute for the universal analytic argument.

value.rationale: The motivating August 2026 paper explicitly poses the exact nonzero-angle second-Hankel extremal behavior, for which its sharpness proof only treats the convex beta=0 case. The endpoint coefficient 11/96 and its explicit family of asymptotic extremizers sharply improve the leading published upper constant 17/144 and quantify approach by a uniform error. The boundary regime is a natural structural limit of the whole angular class and involves a nontrivial sharp Herglotz-moment classification; this is not a routine finite example, relabeling, or tiny incidental numerical improvement.
